## 10. Computational evidence

An exhaustive check on $G = \mathbb{Z}/4$ is small enough to be carried out in exact arithmetic: all characters take values in $\{1, i, -1, -i\}$, so with function values restricted to $\{0, 1, -1, i, -i\}$ the transform lives in the Gaussian integers and every count below is exact rather than numerical.

Enumerating all $5^4 = 625$ such functions:

| experiment | result |
|---|---|
| functions tested / nonzero | 625 / 624 |
| the bound $|\operatorname{supp} f| \cdot |\operatorname{supp}\hat f| \ge 4$ | holds in every case |
| number of extremals in the sample | 48 |
| support-size distribution of extremals (sizes $0,1,2,3,4$) | $0, 16, 16, 0, 16$ |
| every extremal support is a coset (parallelogram closure) | yes |
| every extremal has constant modulus on its support | yes |
| every extremal frequency support is a coset | yes |
| pointwise products of extremals are zero or extremal | yes |
| convolutions of extremals are zero or extremal | yes |
| the non-coset set $\{0,1\}$ as a support | not extremal ($2 \cdot 3 = 6 > 4$) |

Every entry matches the theory. The absence of extremals with support of size $3$ is Theorem 5.7: $3 \nmid 4$. The counts $16$ are also predicted exactly: for size $1$, four positions times four allowed nonzero values; for size $2$, two cosets of $\{0,2\}$ times four values times two characters modulo the annihilator; for size $4$, four characters times four values.

Section 5's separation of the two groups of order four was likewise confirmed by exhaustive enumeration: $\mathbb{Z}/4$ has exactly $2$ extremal supports of size $2$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\times\mathbb{Z}/2$ has exactly $6$.

---

## 11. Discussion

**What the theorems buy.** The classification turns an analytic extremal problem into an arithmetic one. Questions of the form "how sparse can a signal be while having few frequencies?" become questions about the divisor lattice of $N$. On $\mathbb{Z}/p$ the extremal class is trivial (deltas and characters) and every other support size incurs a definite penalty; on $\mathbb{Z}/2^k$ the extremal class is a full chain of subgroups with plentiful worst cases. Group order, not group size, decides how badly the uncertainty principle can be saturated.

**Sharpness of the bound in signal recovery.** In compressed sensing, the uncertainty principle underlies the uniqueness of sparse representations: if $|\operatorname{supp} f| \cdot |\operatorname{supp}\hat f| < N$ for two candidate representations of the same signal, they must coincide. The extremal functions are exactly the boundary cases where such arguments become tight, and Theorem 3.12 says these boundary cases are structured — they are Dirac combs on cosets — so they can be recognised and excluded in $O(|S|^2)$ time by Algorithm 3.

**The role of the abelian hypothesis.** Two ingredients are genuinely abelian: Pontryagin duality (used through $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}| = N$, which we obtain from Plancherel) and the converse of Lagrange's theorem (Theorem 5.6). The latter fails for nonabelian groups, so any nonabelian analogue of Theorem 5.7 must have a different shape; already for $A_5$ one would need to explain the missing "divisor" $30$.

**A remark on proof technique.** Both rigidity results are equality analyses of the triangle inequality, and both use the same lemma — unit-modulus complex numbers whose sum has maximal modulus are all equal. It is the same phenomenon that makes coherence arguments work in analysis: perfect constructive interference is a very strong constraint, and in the presence of a group action it forces homomorphy.

---

## 12. Future directions

**Beyond abelian groups.** Formulate and prove an uncertainty classification on finite nonabelian groups, where the correct notion of "support" on the dual side involves matrix coefficients and the natural extremals should be induced-from-a-subgroup constructions. Theorem 5.6 fails, so the achievable spectrum will not be the divisor set.

**Approximate rigidity.** Both theorems here are exact. The natural stability question is quantitative: if $|\operatorname{supp} f|\cdot|\operatorname{supp}\hat f| \le (1+\varepsilon)N$, must $f$ be $\delta(\varepsilon)$-close (in a suitable norm) to a coset modulation? Section 3's equality analysis is a chain of inequalities each of which admits a stability version, so a quantitative statement should follow with explicit constants; the interesting question is the optimal dependence on $\varepsilon$ and $N$. Similarly, an approximate Poisson pair — one for which the identity holds up to $\varepsilon\|f\|_1$ — should be close to a subgroup/annihilator pair.

**Ring and module versions.** Replace $G$ by a finite module over a ring and $\widehat G$ by its Pontryagin dual; the extremal class should become the class of modulated indicators of submodules, and the spectrum should be the set of submodule orders. The interest is that this set is generally *not* the divisor set.

**Finite-test phenomena.** Corollary 3.8 says Poisson summation is determined by $N$ scalar identities. Which other functional identities in harmonic analysis are determined by finitely many test cases, and with what optimal test families? A minimal test family for the Poisson identity would be an appealing extremal combinatorial problem in its own right.

**Extremal supports as an invariant.** The family of extremal supports separates $\mathbb{Z}/4$ from $\mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$. Is the multiset $\{(d, \#\{\text{extremal supports of size } d\})\}_{d \mid N}$ a complete invariant of a finite abelian group? Equivalently: is a finite abelian group determined by the number of subgroups it has of each order? The question reduces, by the structure theorem, to the case of abelian $p$-groups, where the counts are governed by the partition describing the group.

**Dynamics of convolution.** Theorem 6.5 shows the support size is conserved under convolution powers of an extremal function. Describe the full orbit structure of the convolution dynamics on the extremal class: convolution acts on the parameters $(K, a, \chi, c)$ by join of subgroups, addition of representatives and addition of characters, so the dynamics is a semigroup action on the subgroup lattice — the equilibrium states and their basins are worth mapping out explicitly.

\begin{abstract}

govern the interaction between the transform and the subgroup lattice of $G$: subgroup
indicators attain equality in the Donoho--Stark uncertainty principle

summation formula $N\sum_{x \in H} f = |H| \sum_{\psi \in H^{\perp}} \hat f$.

same object. First, if a nonempty finite $S \subseteq G$ and a finite $T \subseteq \Gh$
satisfy the Poisson identity for \emph{all} test functions, then $S$ is a subgroup and $T$ is
exactly its annihilator; moreover the identity need only be verified on the $N$ Dirac

$s = |\supp f| \nmid N$, and the extremal spectrum theorem, which identifies the achievable
support sizes with the divisors of $N$ on an arbitrary finite abelian group. Consequences
include detection of primality by the extremal class, reconstruction of the group order from
the spectrum, closure of the extremal class under products, convolutions, convolution powers
and the Fourier transform, and the identification of the extremal probability distributions

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{Two ``if'' theorems and two missing converses}

Harmonic analysis on a finite abelian group $G$ of order $N$ is governed by the interaction
between two lattices: the subgroup lattice of $G$ and that of the dual group $\Gh$, matched by
the annihilator correspondence $H \mapsto H^{\perp}$. Two facts sit at the centre.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Fact A (extremality of subgroup indicators).} For $H \le G$ the transform of
$\1_H$ is $|H|\cdot \1_{H^{\perp}}$ and $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}| = N$, so $\1_H$ attains equality
in the Donoho--Stark uncertainty principle. Since scaling, translation and modulation permute
the two supports without changing their sizes, the whole orbit
\[
  f(x) = c\,\chi(x)\,\1_{a+K}(x), \qquad c \ne 0,\ \chi \in \Gh,\ a \in G,\ K \le G,
\]
consists of extremal functions. We call these \emph{coset modulations}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Fact B (Poisson summation).} For $H \le G$ and every $f : G \to \C$,
\[
  N \sum_{x \in H} f(x) = |H| \sum_{\psi \in H^{\perp}} \hat f(\psi).
\]

\medskip
Both are ``if'' statements: a subgroup produces a phenomenon. We show that the phenomenon
produces the subgroup, in both cases, and that the two answers coincide.

\subsection{Main results}

Throughout, $\supp f = \{x \in G : f(x) \ne 0\}$.

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of Poisson summation]\label{thm:main-poisson}
Let $S \subseteq G$ be nonempty and $T \subseteq \Gh$, and suppose that
$N \sum_{x \in S} f(x) = |S| \sum_{\psi \in T} \hat f(\psi)$ for all $f : G \to \C$.
Then $S$ is a subgroup of $G$ and $T = S^{\perp}$. In particular $0 \in S$ and
$|S|\cdot|T| = N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Classification of the Donoho--Stark extremals]\label{thm:main-extremal}
A nonzero $f : G \to \C$ satisfies $|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| = N$ if and only if $f$ is a
coset modulation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extremal spectrum]\label{thm:main-spectrum}
For $d \in \N$, there is a nonzero extremal $f$ on $G$ with $|\supp f| = d$ if and only if
$d \mid N$. More precisely, a pair $(s,t)$ occurs as $(|\supp f|, |\supp\hat f|)$ for an
extremal $f$ if and only if $st = N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extremal probability distributions]\label{thm:main-prob}
A probability distribution on $G$ attaining equality in the uncertainty principle is the
uniform distribution on a coset of a subgroup.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Context}
The inequality $|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| \ge N$ is the discrete uncertainty principle of
Donoho and Stark, the combinatorial backbone of sparse recovery: a nonzero signal cannot be
simultaneously sparse in space and in frequency. Understanding the equality case is
understanding the worst case for such guarantees, and the results below convert that analytic
extremal problem into an arithmetic one governed by the factorisation of $N$.

\section{Setting and conventions}

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively, $N := |G|$, and
$\Gh := \Hom(G, \C^{\times})$ its character group, also written additively:
$(\psi + \chi)(x) = \psi(x)\chi(x)$ and $(\psi - \chi)(x) = \psi(x)/\chi(x)$. Every character
is unimodular and $|\Gh| = N$.

\begin{definition}
For $f : G \to \C$, $\displaystyle \hat f(\psi) := \sum_{x \in G} \overline{\psi(x)} f(x)$,
$\psi \in \Gh$.
\end{definition}

We use the following standard facts.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Character orthogonality over a subgroup.} For $H \le G$,
  $\sum_{x \in H}\psi(x) = |H|$ if $\psi \in H^{\perp} := \{\psi : \psi|_H \equiv 1\}$, and
  $0$ otherwise. (Translation by $x_0 \in H$ with $\psi(x_0)\ne1$ permutes $H$, so
  $(\psi(x_0)-1)\sum_{x \in H}\psi(x) = 0$.)
  \item \emph{Inversion.} $f(x) = \frac1N \sum_{\psi} \psi(x)\hat f(\psi)$.
  \item \emph{Plancherel.} $\sum_{\psi}|\hat f(\psi)|^2 = N\sum_x |f(x)|^2$.
  \item \emph{Convolution.} $(u*v)(x) := \sum_y u(y)v(x-y)$ satisfies
  $\widehat{u*v} = \hat u \hat v$.
  \item \emph{Dirac functions.} $\widehat{\delta_y}(\psi) = \overline{\psi(y)}$.
  \item \emph{Donoho--Stark.} $|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| \ge N$ for $f \ne 0$.
\end{itemize}

\begin{definition}
The \emph{translate} is $(T_a f)(x) := f(x-a)$ and the \emph{modulate} is
$(M_\chi f)(x) := \chi(x) f(x)$. A function $f$ is \emph{extremal} if
$|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| = N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetries}
$\widehat{T_a f}(\psi) = \overline{\psi(a)}\hat f(\psi)$ and
$\widehat{M_\chi f}(\psi) = \hat f(\psi - \chi)$. Consequently scaling by $c \ne 0$,
translation and modulation all preserve $|\supp f|$ and $|\supp \hat f|$, so the extremal set
is invariant under the three symmetries.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Reindex the defining sum by $x \mapsto x + a$ for the first identity, and use
$\overline{(\psi-\chi)(x)} = \overline{\psi(x)}\chi(x)$ for the second. Translation permutes
$\supp f$ and multiplies $\hat f$ pointwise by a unimodular factor; modulation fixes $\supp f$
and translates $\supp\hat f$ inside $\Gh$.
\end{proof}

\section{The two rigidity theorems}

\subsection{Equality in the triangle inequality}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:tri1}
Let $z_i \in \C$, $i \in s$ finite, with $|z_i| = 1$ and $\sum_{i \in s} z_i = |s|$. Then
$z_i = 1$ for all $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Taking real parts, $\sum_i \operatorname{Re} z_i = |s|$ while $\operatorname{Re} z_i \le 1$
termwise, so $\operatorname{Re}z_i = 1$ for every $i$; with $|z_i| = 1$ this gives
$\operatorname{Im} z_i = 0$ and $z_i = 1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:tri2}
Let $z_i$, $i \in s$, satisfy $|z_i| = M > 0$ and $\bigl|\sum_i z_i\bigr| = |s| M$. Then all
$z_i$ are equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put $\Sigma := \sum_i z_i \ne 0$ and $w_i := \overline{\Sigma}z_i/(|\Sigma| M)$. Then
$|w_i| = 1$ and $\sum_i w_i = |\Sigma|^2/(|\Sigma| M) = |\Sigma|/M = |s|$, so all $w_i = 1$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:tri1}; hence $\overline\Sigma z_i$ is independent of $i$, and cancelling
$\overline\Sigma$ gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Rigidity of Poisson summation}

\begin{definition}
A pair $(S,T)$ with $S \subseteq G$, $T \subseteq \Gh$ is a \emph{Poisson pair} if
$N\sum_{x\in S} f(x) = |S| \sum_{\psi \in T} \hat f(\psi)$ for every $f : G \to \C$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Dirac test]\label{lem:dirac}
If $(S,T)$ is a Poisson pair, then $N\,\1_S(y) = |S|\sum_{\psi \in T} \psi(y)$ for all
$y \in G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Apply the definition to $f = \delta_y$ and conjugate the resulting scalar identity, whose left
side is real.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:poisson-count}
If $(S,T)$ is a Poisson pair with $S \ne \emptyset$ then $0 \in S$ and $|S|\cdot|T| = N$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set $y=0$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:dirac}: $N \1_S(0) = |S|\,|T|$. If $0 \notin S$ then $T$ is empty
and Lemma~\ref{lem:dirac} forces $S = \emptyset$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}
For $T \subseteq \Gh$, the \emph{pre-annihilator} is
${}^{\perp}T := \{y \in G : \psi(y) = 1 \text{ for all } \psi \in T\}$; it is a subgroup of
$G$, being an intersection of kernels.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Annihilator count]\label{prop:ann}
For $H \le G$ we have $\widehat{\1_H} = |H| \cdot \1_{H^{\perp}}$ and
$|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}| = N$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is character orthogonality applied to $-\psi$, using
$\overline{\psi(x)} = (-\psi)(x)$ and $-\psi \in H^{\perp} \iff \psi \in H^{\perp}$. Plancherel
for $\1_H$ then reads $|H^{\perp}|\,|H|^2 = N |H|$, and $|H| > 0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem~\ref{thm:main-poisson}]\label{thm:poisson-converse}
Let $(S,T)$ be a Poisson pair with $S$ nonempty. Then $S = {}^{\perp}T$ is a subgroup of $G$
and $T = S^{\perp}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:poisson-count}, $N = |S||T|$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:dirac} becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:star}
  \sum_{\psi \in T}\psi(y) = |T| \cdot \1_S(y), \qquad y \in G.
\end{equation}
If $y \in S$, the left side of \eqref{eq:star} is a sum of $|T|$ unimodular numbers equal to
$|T|$, so $\psi(y) = 1$ for all $\psi \in T$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:tri1}, i.e.\ $y \in {}^{\perp}T$.
Conversely if $y \in {}^{\perp}T$ then the left side equals $|T| > 0$, forcing $y \in S$. Hence
$S = {}^{\perp}T$ is a subgroup. Every $\psi \in T$ is trivial on $S$, so $T \subseteq
S^{\perp}$, and $|S^{\perp}| = N/|S| = |T|$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:ann}, whence equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Poisson summation is a finite test]\label{cor:finite-test}
If the Poisson identity for $(S,T)$ holds for the $N$ Dirac functions $\delta_y$, it holds for
every $f$, and hence Theorem~\ref{thm:poisson-converse} applies.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Both sides are $\C$-linear in $f$, and the $\delta_y$ span $\C^G$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The equality analysis behind the uncertainty principle}

\begin{theorem}[Flatness and alignment]\label{thm:flat}
Let $f \ne 0$ be extremal. Then there is $M > 0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $|f(x)| = M$ for all $x \in \supp f$; and
  \item for every $\psi \in \supp \hat f$, the quantity $\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$ is the same
  for all $x \in \supp f$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $M := \max_x |f(x)|$, attained at $m$, and $\Sigma := \sum_{x \in \supp f}|f(x)|$. Then
$\Sigma \le |\supp f| M$; $|\hat f(\psi)| \le \Sigma$ for all $\psi$ because characters are
unimodular; and inversion at $m$ restricted to $\supp \hat f$ gives
$N M \le \sum_{\psi \in \supp \hat f} |\hat f(\psi)|$. Chaining,
\[
  N M \;\le\; \sum_{\psi \in \supp\hat f}|\hat f(\psi)| \;\le\; |\supp\hat f|\,\Sigma
  \;\le\; |\supp\hat f|\,|\supp f|\,M \;=\; NM,
\]
so all inequalities are equalities. The first collapse gives $|f| \equiv M$ on $\supp f$. The
last-but-one gives $|\hat f(\psi)| = \Sigma = |\supp f| M$ for every $\psi \in \supp\hat f$;
since $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{x \in \supp f}\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$ is a sum of $|\supp f|$
terms of modulus $M$ whose total modulus is $|\supp f| M$, Lemma~\ref{lem:tri2} makes those
terms equal.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The structure theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem~\ref{thm:main-extremal}]\label{thm:structure}
A nonzero $f : G \to \C$ is extremal if and only if there are $K \le G$, $\chi \in \Gh$,
$a \in G$ and $c \ne 0$ with $f(x) = c\,\chi(x)$ for $x - a \in K$ and $f(x) = 0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$(\Leftarrow)$ Such an $f$ is $c\,M_\chi T_a \1_K$; $\1_K$ is extremal by
Proposition~\ref{prop:ann}, and extremality survives the three symmetries by
Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetries}.

$(\Rightarrow)$ Pick $a \in \supp f$ and $\psi_0 \in \supp \hat f$; both supports are nonempty
since $f \ne 0$ and the transform is injective. Let $M$, flatness and alignment be as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:flat}.

\emph{Step 1.} For $\psi \in \supp\hat f$ and $x \in \supp f$, alignment gives
$\overline{\psi(x)}f(x) = \overline{\psi(a)}f(a)$; multiplying by $\psi(x)$ and using
$\psi(x)\overline{\psi(x)} = 1$, $\overline{\psi(a)} = \psi(a)^{-1}$ and
$\psi(x)\psi(a)^{-1} = \psi(x-a)$ yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:values}
  f(x) = \psi(x-a) f(a).
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 2.} Let $K := \langle\, x - a : x \in \supp f \,\rangle$. Comparing
\eqref{eq:values} for $\psi$ and $\psi_0$ and cancelling $f(a)\ne 0$ gives
$\psi(x-a) = \psi_0(x-a)$. The set $\{g : \psi(g) = \psi_0(g)\}$ is a subgroup containing all
generators of $K$, so every $\psi \in \supp\hat f$ agrees with $\psi_0$ on $K$.

\emph{Step 3.} Hence $\supp f \subseteq a+K$, so $|\supp f| \le |K|$; and
$\psi \mapsto \psi-\psi_0$ maps $\supp \hat f$ injectively into $K^{\perp}$, so
$|\supp\hat f| \le |K^{\perp}|$.

\emph{Step 4.} Multiplying, $N = |\supp f|\,|\supp\hat f| \le |K|\,|K^{\perp}| = N$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:ann}, so both inequalities are equalities; in particular
$\supp f = a + K$ exactly.

\emph{Step 5.} With $c := f(a)\overline{\psi_0(a)} \ne 0$ and $\chi := \psi_0$,
\eqref{eq:values} gives $f(x) = c\,\chi(x)$ on $a + K$, and $f$ vanishes off $a+K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:coset}
The support of an extremal function is a coset of a subgroup and its frequency support is a
coset of the annihilator of that subgroup. In particular $\supp f$ is closed under the
parallelogram operation $(x,y,z)\mapsto x-y+z$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Prime order rigidity]
If $|G| = p$ is prime and $f\ne0$ is extremal, then $f = c\,\delta_a$ for some $a$ and
$c \ne 0$, or $f = c\,\chi$ for some character $\chi$ and $c \ne 0$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Uniqueness and the combinatorial description of the subgroup}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:diffset}
If $S = a + K$ for a subgroup $K$, then $K = S - S := \{x-y : x,y \in S\}$. Consequently the
pair $(K, a+K)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:structure} is unique: $K$ absolutely, and $a$ modulo $K$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$(a+k)-(a+k') = k - k' \in K$ and $k = (a+k)-a$, so $S - S = K$; uniqueness follows since the
difference set does not refer to $K$ or $a$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For extremal $f \ne 0$, the subgroup of Theorem~\ref{thm:structure} equals
$\supp f - \supp f$: an analytically defined object with a purely combinatorial description.
\end{corollary}

\section{Arithmetic of the extremal class}

\begin{theorem}[Lagrange rigidity]\label{thm:lagrange}
Let $f\ne0$ be extremal. Then $|\supp f|$ and $|\supp\hat f|$ both divide $N$, and
$|\supp \hat f| = N/|\supp f|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\supp f$ is a coset of a subgroup $K$ by Corollary~\ref{cor:coset}, so $|\supp f| = |K|$
divides $N$ by Lagrange's theorem; the rest is extremality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uncertainty gap]\label{thm:gap}
Let $f \ne 0$ and $s := |\supp f|$. If $s \nmid N$ then
\[
  |\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| \;\ge\; N + \bigl(s - (N \bmod s)\bigr) \;\ge\; N+1,
\]
equivalently $|\supp \hat f| \ge \lceil N/s\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $N = sq + r$ with $0 < r < s$. Donoho--Stark gives $st \ge N$ with
$t := |\supp\hat f|$, so $t \ge q+1$; hence $st \ge sq + s = N - r + s$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}
The \emph{extremal spectrum} of $G$ is
$\Spec(G) := \{d \in \N : \exists\, f \ne 0 \text{ extremal},\ |\supp f| = d\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:spec-subgroups}
$\Spec(G)$ is exactly the set of subgroup orders of $G$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Converse of Lagrange for finite abelian groups]\label{thm:cauchy}
If $A$ is a finite abelian group and $d \mid |A|$, then $A$ has a subgroup of order $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Induct on $|A|$. For $d = 1$ take the trivial subgroup. Otherwise choose a prime $p \mid d$;
then $p \mid |A|$, so by Cauchy's theorem there is a subgroup $C \le A$ of order $p$. In
$A/C$, of order $|A|/p$, the divisor $d/p$ is realised by a subgroup $\bar B$ by induction, and
the preimage of $\bar B$ in $A$ has order $p \cdot (d/p) = d$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
This fails for general finite groups: $|A_5| = 60$ but $A_5$ has no subgroup of order $30$.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem~\ref{thm:main-spectrum}; extremal spectrum theorem]\label{thm:spectrum}
For any finite abelian $G$ and $d \in \N$, $d \in \Spec(G)$ if and only if $d \mid N$. The
same holds on the frequency side, and a pair $(s,t)$ occurs as $(|\supp f|,|\supp\hat f|)$ for
an extremal $f$ if and only if $st = N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine Proposition~\ref{prop:spec-subgroups} with Lagrange's theorem for necessity and with
Theorem~\ref{thm:cauchy} for sufficiency; the pair statement then follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrange}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Primality is visible in the extremal class]
$N$ is prime if and only if $N > 1$ and every nonzero extremal $f$ on $G$ satisfies
$|\supp f| \in \{1, N\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Necessity is Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrange}. For sufficiency, let $d \mid N$; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:spectrum} some extremal has support size $d$, so $d \in \{1,N\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reconstruction and its ceiling]
For finite abelian $G, G'$, one has $\Spec(G) = \Spec(G')$ if and only if $|G| = |G'|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:spectrum} the spectrum is the divisor set of the order, and a positive
integer is determined by its divisor set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Supports of extremals are exactly the cosets]\label{thm:supports}
A nonempty $S \subseteq G$ equals $\supp f$ for some extremal $f$ if and only if $S$ is a coset
of a subgroup, equivalently if and only if $S$ is closed under $(x,y,z) \mapsto x-y+z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Necessity is Corollary~\ref{cor:coset}; sufficiency is Theorem~\ref{thm:structure} applied to
$T_a \1_K$. A coset is clearly parallelogram-closed. Conversely, if $S \ne \emptyset$ is
parallelogram-closed and $a \in S$, put $K := S - a$: then $0 \in K$; for $x,y \in S$ we have
$x - a + y \in S$, so $(x-a)+(y-a) \in K$; and $a - x + a \in S$, so $-(x-a) \in K$. Thus $K$
is a subgroup and $S = a+K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}
$\Z/4$ and $\Z/2\times\Z/2$ have the same extremal spectrum $\{1,2,4\}$, but $\Z/4$ has
exactly $2$ extremal supports of size $2$ and the Klein group has $6$ (two cosets for each of
its three subgroups of order $2$). Exhaustive enumeration confirms both counts, so the family
of extremal supports separates the two groups while the spectrum does not.
\end{example}

\section{The extremal class is an algebra}

\begin{lemma}[Transform of a coset modulation]\label{lem:dft-coset}
For $f = c\,M_\chi T_a \1_K$ with $c \ne 0$,
\[
  \hat f(\psi) = \begin{cases}
    c\;\overline{(\psi-\chi)(a)}\;|K|, & \psi - \chi \in K^{\perp},\\
    0, & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}
\]
In particular the transform of a coset modulation is a coset modulation on the dual group, with
subgroup $K^{\perp}$ and representative $\chi$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Intersecting cosets]\label{lem:inter}
Let $K,K' \le G$ and suppose $b - a \in K$ and $b - a' \in K'$. Then for all $x$,
$\bigl(x - a \in K \text{ and } x - a' \in K'\bigr) \iff x - b \in K \cap K'$. Hence the
intersection of a coset of $K$ and a coset of $K'$ is empty or a coset of $K \cap K'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Closure under products]\label{thm:mul}
If $u,v \ne 0$ are extremal, then $uv$ is identically zero or extremal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $u = c\chi\1_{a+K}$ and $v = c'\chi'\1_{a'+K'}$. If the cosets are disjoint then
$uv \equiv 0$; otherwise, choosing $b$ in the intersection, Lemma~\ref{lem:inter} identifies
$uv$ with $cc'(\chi+\chi')\1_{b+(K\cap K')}$, extremal by Theorem~\ref{thm:structure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Closure under convolution]\label{thm:conv}
If $u,v \ne 0$ are extremal, then $u*v$ is identically zero or extremal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
On the frequency side $\widehat{u*v} = \hat u \hat v$, and each factor is supported on a coset
of an annihilator by Lemma~\ref{lem:dft-coset}; by Lemma~\ref{lem:inter} in the dual group the
frequency support is empty or a coset of $K^{\perp}\cap K'^{\perp} = (K+K')^{\perp}$, so
$|\supp\widehat{u*v}| \le |(K+K')^{\perp}|$. On the space side
$\supp(u*v) \subseteq (a+a') + (K+K')$, so $|\supp(u*v)| \le |K+K'|$. The two bounds multiply
to $N$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:ann}, while Donoho--Stark bounds the actual product below by
$N$; hence equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Convolution powers]
Set $f^{*0} := \delta_0$ and $f^{*(k+1)} := f * f^{*k}$. If $f \ne 0$ then $f^{*k}\ne0$ for all
$k$, since $\widehat{f^{*k}} = (\hat f)^k$. If $f$ is extremal then so is $f^{*k}$ for every
$k \ge 1$, and $|\supp f^{*k}| = |\supp f|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Induction with Theorem~\ref{thm:conv}; the frequency support satisfies
$\supp (\hat f)^k = \supp \hat f$, so its size is conserved and extremality pins the space
support size.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier invariance]
If $f$ is extremal on $G$ then $\hat f$ is extremal on $\Gh$, i.e.\
$|\supp \hat f| \cdot |\supp \widehat{\hat f}| = |\Gh| = N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Under the Pontryagin identification $\widehat{\Gh} \cong G$ one has $\widehat{\hat f} = N\,f
\circ (-\mathrm{id})$, so $|\supp \widehat{\hat f}| = |\supp f|$; combine with $|\Gh| = N$.
\end{proof}

\section{The two rigidities are one}

\begin{theorem}
Let $(S,T)$ be a Poisson pair with $S$ nonempty. Then $S = \supp f$ and $T = \supp \hat f$ for
the extremal function $f = \1_S$, the subgroup witnessing the pair is unique, and $|S| \mid N$.
Conversely, for every subgroup $H \le G$ the pair $(H, H^{\perp})$ is a Poisson pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Poisson spectrum]
A number $d$ is the size of a nonempty set carrying a Poisson summation formula on $G$ if and
only if $d \mid N$.
\end{theorem}

Thus the Poisson pairs on $G$ are indexed exactly by the subgroups of $G$, the extremal
functions by quadruples (subgroup, coset representative, character, scalar), and the map
``extremal function $\mapsto$ support pair'' carries the latter onto the former.

\section{Extremal probability distributions}

\begin{theorem}[Theorem~\ref{thm:main-prob}]
Let $p : G \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $p \ge 0$ and $\sum_x p(x) = 1$, and suppose $p$, viewed as
a complex-valued function, is extremal. Then there are $a \in G$ and $K \le G$ with
$p = \frac{1}{|K|}\1_{a+K}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$p \ne 0$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:structure} gives $p = c\,\chi\,\1_{a+K}$ with $c \ne 0$. Since
$|\chi| \equiv 1$, flatness gives $|p(x)| = |c|$ on the support, and $p \ge 0$ upgrades this to
$p(x) = |c|$ there. Summing, $|K|\,|c| = 1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
The minimum-uncertainty distributions on $G$ are exactly the uniform distributions on cosets of
subgroups; their support sizes divide $N$. On a group of prime order they are the point masses
and the uniform distribution on $G$, and nothing else.
\end{corollary}

\section{Algorithms}

Let $G = \Z/n_1 \times \cdots \times \Z/n_r$ with $N = \prod_j n_j$; characters are indexed by
$k \in G$ via $\psi_k(x) = \exp(2\pi i \sum_j k_j x_j / n_j)$.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Uncertainty audit.} Compute $\hat f$ in $O(N^2)$ (or $O(N\log N)$ by a
  mixed-radix FFT), count both supports with a numerical tolerance, and compare the product
  with $N$.
  \item \emph{Structure extraction.} Given an extremal $f$, set $S := \supp f$, pick $a \in S$,
  and return $K := S - a$; the character is read off from $f(x)/f(a) = \chi(x-a)$ and the
  scalar from $c = f(a)\overline{\chi(a)}$. Cost $O(|S|)$ beyond the transform.
  \item \emph{Coset test.} Decide whether a nonempty $S$ is an extremal support by testing
  parallelogram closure, in $O(|S|^2)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:supports}).
  \item \emph{Poisson pair verification.} Verify only the $N$ Dirac identities
  $N\1_S(y) = |S|\sum_{\psi \in T}\psi(y)$; by Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-test} this certifies
  the identity for all test functions. Cost $O(N|T|)$.
  \item \emph{Extremal spectrum.} Enumerate the divisors of $N$ in $O(\sqrt N)$
  (Theorem~\ref{thm:spectrum}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Computational evidence}

On $G = \Z/4$ all characters take values in $\{1,i,-1,-i\}$, so with function values restricted
to $\{0,1,-1,i,-i\}$ the transform lives in the Gaussian integers and the following counts are
exact.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
experiment & result \\
\midrule
functions tested / nonzero & 625 / 624 \\
$|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\hat f| \ge 4$ & holds in every case \\
number of extremals & 48 \\
support-size distribution (sizes $0,1,2,3,4$) & $0,16,16,0,16$ \\
every extremal support is a coset & yes \\
every extremal has constant modulus on its support & yes \\
every extremal frequency support is a coset & yes \\
products of extremals are zero or extremal & yes \\
convolutions of extremals are zero or extremal & yes \\
the set $\{0,1\}$ as a support & not extremal ($2\cdot3 = 6 > 4$) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The absence of extremals of support size $3$ is exactly Theorem~\ref{thm:spectrum}, since
$3 \nmid 4$; and the three counts $16$ are predicted precisely by the classification
($4$ positions $\times$ $4$ values; $2$ cosets $\times$ $4$ values $\times$ $2$ characters
modulo the annihilator; $4$ characters $\times$ $4$ values).

\section{Discussion and future directions}

The classification turns an analytic extremal problem into an arithmetic one: on $\Z/p$ the
extremal class is trivial and every intermediate support size incurs the gap of
Theorem~\ref{thm:gap}, while on $\Z/2^k$ it is a full chain of subgroups with plentiful
saturating examples. Two ingredients are genuinely abelian: Pontryagin duality, used through
$|H|\,|H^{\perp}| = N$, and the converse of Lagrange's theorem.

Natural continuations include: a nonabelian analogue, where the extremals should be
induced-from-a-subgroup constructions and the spectrum is no longer the divisor set; a
quantitative stability theory (if $|\supp f|\,|\supp \hat f| \le (1+\varepsilon)N$, how close
must $f$ be to a coset modulation?); module-theoretic versions in which the spectrum becomes
the set of submodule orders; minimal test families for identities such as Poisson summation,
of which Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-test} gives one of size $N$; the question of whether the
counting function $d \mapsto \#\{\text{extremal supports of size } d\}$ is a complete invariant
of a finite abelian group; and an explicit description of the convolution dynamics on the
extremal class, which acts on the parameters $(K,a,\chi,c)$ by join of subgroups and addition
of representatives and characters.

Minimum Uncertainty Is a Subgroup
=================================

Numerical demonstrations of the classification of the extremals of the
Donoho-Stark uncertainty principle on a finite abelian group, and of the
rigidity of finite Poisson summation.

Everything is implemented from scratch with the standard library only.

A finite abelian group is represented as a tuple of moduli, e.g.

    (12,)      is  Z/12
    (2, 2)     is  Z/2 x Z/2
    (6, 2)     is  Z/6 x Z/2

Its elements are tuples of residues, and the character indexed by k is

    psi_k(x) = exp( 2*pi*i * sum_j k_j x_j / n_j ).

The discrete Fourier transform used throughout is

    fhat(psi) = sum_x conj(psi(x)) f(x),

with inversion f(x) = (1/N) sum_psi psi(x) fhat(psi) and Plancherel
sum_psi |fhat(psi)|^2 = N sum_x |f(x)|^2.

The results demonstrated:

  1. Coset modulations c * chi * 1_{a+K} are extremal:
     |supp f| * |supp fhat| = |G|.
  2. Conversely, every extremal function is a coset modulation, and its
     subgroup is the difference set of its support.
  3. The extremal spectrum of G is exactly the divisor set of |G|.
  4. If |supp f| does not divide |G| the uncertainty product overshoots by
     at least |supp f| - (|G| mod |supp f|).
  5. Poisson summation holds exactly for (subgroup, annihilator) pairs, and
     the |G| Dirac identities already certify it.
  6. The extremal class is closed under pointwise products and convolutions.
  7. An extremal probability distribution is uniform on a coset.
  8. Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/2 have the same extremal spectrum but different
     families of extremal supports.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Elem = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Func = Dict[Elem, complex]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Group arithmetic and characters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elem]:
    """All elements of Z/n_1 x ... x Z/n_r, in lexicographic order."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The order |G| of the group."""
    n = 1
    for m in group:
        n *= m
    return n


def add(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group addition."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def sub(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group subtraction."""
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def zero(group: Group) -> Elem:
    """The neutral element."""
    return tuple(0 for _ in group)


def character(group: Group, k: Elem, x: Elem) -> complex:
    """The character psi_k evaluated at x: exp(2*pi*i * sum k_j x_j / n_j)."""
    phase = sum(2.0 * cmath.pi * (kj * xj) / nj for kj, xj, nj in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * phase)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The discrete Fourier transform
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    """fhat(k) = sum_x conj(psi_k(x)) f(x), indexed by the dual element k."""
    els = elements(group)
    out: Func = {}
    for k in els:
        total = 0j
        for x in els:
            fx = f.get(x, 0j)
            if fx != 0:
                total += character(group, k, x).conjugate() * fx
        out[k] = total
    return out


def idft(group: Group, fhat: Func) -> Func:
    """Inverse transform: f(x) = (1/N) sum_k psi_k(x) fhat(k)."""
    els = elements(group)
    n = order(group)
    return {
        x: sum(character(group, k, x) * fhat.get(k, 0j) for k in els) / n for x in els
    }


def support(f: Func, tol: float = TOL) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The set of points where f is (numerically) nonzero."""
    return {x for x, v in f.items() if abs(v) > tol}


def uncertainty_product(group: Group, f: Func) -> int:
    """|supp f| * |supp fhat|."""
    return len(support(f)) * len(support(dft(group, f)))


def is_extremal(group: Group, f: Func) -> bool:
    """True when |supp f| * |supp fhat| = |G| (and f is nonzero)."""
    if not support(f):
        return False
    return uncertainty_product(group, f) == order(group)


def convolve(group: Group, u: Func, v: Func) -> Func:
    """(u * v)(x) = sum_y u(y) v(x - y)."""
    els = elements(group)
    return {
        x: sum(u.get(y, 0j) * v.get(sub(group, x, y), 0j) for y in els) for x in els
    }


def pointwise(u: Func, v: Func) -> Func:
    """Pointwise product."""
    return {x: u.get(x, 0j) * v.get(x, 0j) for x in set(u) | set(v)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subgroups, cosets, coset modulations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def subgroup_generated(group: Group, gens: Iterable[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The subgroup of G generated by the given elements (closure by BFS)."""
    seen: Set[Elem] = {zero(group)}
    frontier: List[Elem] = [zero(group)]
    gens = list(gens)
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for g in gens:
            y = add(group, x, g)
            if y not in seen:
                seen.add(y)
                frontier.append(y)
    return seen


def all_subgroups(group: Group) -> List[Set[Elem]]:
    """All subgroups of G, obtained by closing every subset of generators
    of size at most the rank + 1 (exhaustive for the small groups used here)."""
    els = elements(group)
    found: Set[frozenset] = set()
    for r in range(0, min(3, len(els)) + 1):
        for gens in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            found.add(frozenset(subgroup_generated(group, gens)))
    return [set(s) for s in sorted(found, key=lambda s: (len(s), sorted(s)))]


def annihilator(group: Group, subgroup: Set[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """K^perp = { k : psi_k(x) = 1 for all x in K }, as a set of dual indices."""
    return {
        k
        for k in elements(group)
        if all(abs(character(group, k, x) - 1.0) < TOL for x in subgroup)
    }


def coset_modulation(
    group: Group, subgroup: Set[Elem], a: Elem, chi: Elem, c: complex
) -> Func:
    """f(x) = c * psi_chi(x) for x in a + K, and 0 elsewhere."""
    cos = {add(group, a, k) for k in subgroup}
    return {
        x: (c * character(group, chi, x) if x in cos else 0j) for x in elements(group)
    }


def difference_set(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """S - S = { x - y : x, y in S }."""
    return {sub(group, x, y) for x in s for y in s}


def is_coset(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """A nonempty S is a coset iff |S - S| = |S| (equivalently, iff S is
    closed under the parallelogram operation (x, y, z) -> x - y + z)."""
    return bool(s) and len(difference_set(group, s)) == len(s)


def is_parallelogram_closed(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """Direct test of closure under (x, y, z) -> x - y + z."""
    return bool(s) and all(
        add(group, sub(group, x, y), z) in s for x in s for y in s for z in s
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structure extraction (Algorithm 2 of the paper)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def extract_structure(
    group: Group, f: Func
) -> Optional[Tuple[Set[Elem], Elem, Elem, complex]]:
    """For an extremal f, recover (K, a, chi, c) with f = c * psi_chi * 1_{a+K}.

    Returns None if f is not extremal.  The subgroup is recovered purely
    combinatorially, as the difference set of the support; the character index
    is then found by matching phases on the support.
    """
    if not is_extremal(group, f):
        return None
    s = support(f)
    a = sorted(s)[0]
    k_sub = difference_set(group, s)
    c_times_chi_a = f[a]
    for chi in elements(group):
        c = c_times_chi_a * character(group, chi, a).conjugate()
        candidate = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, a, chi, c)
        if all(abs(candidate[x] - f.get(x, 0j)) < 1e-7 for x in elements(group)):
            return k_sub, a, chi, c
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Poisson pairs (Definition 3.3, Lemma 3.4, Corollary 3.8)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def poisson_holds_for(group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem], f: Func) -> bool:
    """Check N * sum_{x in S} f(x) = |S| * sum_{k in T} fhat(k) for one f."""
    n = order(group)
    fhat = dft(group, f)
    lhs = n * sum(f.get(x, 0j) for x in s)
    rhs = len(s) * sum(fhat[k] for k in t)
    return abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-7


def poisson_dirac_test(group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """The finite certificate: check only the |G| Dirac identities
    N * 1_S(y) = |S| * sum_{k in T} psi_k(y)."""
    n = order(group)
    for y in elements(group):
        lhs = n * (1.0 if y in s else 0.0)
        rhs = len(s) * sum(character(group, k, y) for k in t)
        if abs(lhs - rhs) > 1e-7:
            return False
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def divisors(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """All positive divisors of n, ascending."""
    return [d for d in range(1, n + 1) if n % d == 0]


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 1: coset modulations saturate the uncertainty principle
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_coset_modulations_are_extremal() -> None:
    banner("1. Coset modulations attain equality:  |supp f| * |supp fhat| = |G|")
    group: Group = (12,)
    n = order(group)
    print(f"G = Z/12,  |G| = {n}\n")
    print(f"{'subgroup K':<28}{'a':<8}{'chi':<7}{'|supp f|':>9}{'|supp fhat|':>13}"
          f"{'product':>9}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for k_sub in all_subgroups(group):
        a: Elem = (1,)
        chi: Elem = (5,)
        f = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, a, chi, 2 + 1j)
        sf, sh = len(support(f)), len(support(dft(group, f)))
        label = "{" + ",".join(str(x[0]) for x in sorted(k_sub)) + "}"
        if len(label) > 26:
            label = label[:23] + "...}"
        print(f"{label:<28}{a[0]:<8}{chi[0]:<7}{sf:>9}{sh:>13}{sf * sh:>9}")
    print("\nEvery product equals |G| = 12, as the classification predicts.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 2: exhaustive verification on Z/4
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_exhaustive_z4() -> None:
    banner("2. Exhaustive census on Z/4 over the values {0, 1, -1, i, -i}")
    group: Group = (4,)
    els = elements(group)
    values: Sequence[complex] = (0j, 1 + 0j, -1 + 0j, 1j, -1j)

    total = 0
    nonzero = 0
    bound_ok = True
    extremals: List[Func] = []
    size_hist: Dict[int, int] = {d: 0 for d in range(5)}

    for combo in itertools.product(values, repeat=len(els)):
        f: Func = dict(zip(els, combo))
        total += 1
        s = support(f)
        if not s:
            continue
        nonzero += 1
        prod = uncertainty_product(group, f)
        if prod < 4:
            bound_ok = False
        if prod == 4:
            extremals.append(f)
            size_hist[len(s)] += 1

    print(f"functions tested / nonzero            : {total} / {nonzero}")
    print(f"uncertainty bound |supp f||supp fhat| >= 4 holds everywhere : {bound_ok}")
    print(f"number of extremals                   : {len(extremals)}")
    print("support-size distribution of extremals: "
          + ", ".join(f"size {d}: {size_hist[d]}" for d in range(5)))
    print("  (no extremal of support size 3, because 3 does not divide 4)")

    all_cosets = all(is_coset(group, support(f)) for f in extremals)
    flat = all(
        len({round(abs(f[x]), 9) for x in support(f)}) == 1 for f in extremals
    )
    freq_cosets = all(
        is_coset(group, support(dft(group, f))) for f in extremals
    )
    print(f"every extremal support is a coset     : {all_cosets}")
    print(f"every extremal is flat on its support : {flat}")
    print(f"every frequency support is a coset    : {freq_cosets}")

    bad: Func = {(0,): 1 + 0j, (1,): 1 + 0j, (2,): 0j, (3,): 0j}
    print(f"\nthe non-coset support {{0,1}}: product = "
          f"{uncertainty_product(group, bad)} > 4, so not extremal")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 3: the extremal spectrum is the divisor set
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_extremal_spectrum() -> None:
    banner("3. The extremal spectrum of G equals the divisor set of |G|")
    for group in [(4,), (2, 2), (6,), (12,), (6, 2)]:
        n = order(group)
        achievable = sorted({len(k) for k in all_subgroups(group)})
        # realise each size by an explicit extremal function and check it
        realised = []
        for k_sub in all_subgroups(group):
            f = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, zero(group), zero(group), 1 + 0j)
            if is_extremal(group, f):
                realised.append(len(k_sub))
        name = " x ".join(f"Z/{m}" for m in group)
        print(f"{name:<14} |G| = {n:>3}   subgroup orders {achievable}"
              f"   divisors {divisors(n)}")
        assert achievable == divisors(n) == sorted(set(realised))
    print("\nEvery divisor is realised by an explicit extremal function, and no"
          "\nother size occurs -- the extremal spectrum theorem.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 4: the gap when the support size does not divide |G|
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_uncertainty_gap() -> None:
    banner("4. The uncertainty gap when |supp f| does not divide |G|")
    group: Group = (12,)
    n = order(group)
    print("G = Z/12.  For each support size s, the sharpened bound is")
    print("    s * |supp fhat| >= N + (s - N mod s)  when s does not divide N.\n")

def demo_algebra_closure() -> None:
    banner("7. Products and convolutions of extremals are zero or extremal")
    group: Group = (12,)
    subs = all_subgroups(group)
    import random

    random.seed(1234)

    pairs = 0
    prod_zero = 0
    conv_zero = 0
    prod_ok = 0
    conv_ok = 0
    for _ in range(60):
        k1 = random.choice(subs)
        k2 = random.choice(subs)
        u = coset_modulation(
            group, k1, random.choice(elements(group)),
            random.choice(elements(group)), complex(random.uniform(0.5, 2))
        )

            group, k2, random.choice(elements(group)),
            random.choice(elements(group)), complex(0, random.uniform(0.5, 2))
        )
        pairs += 1

        w = pointwise(u, v)
        if not support(w):
            prod_zero += 1
        elif is_extremal(group, w):
            prod_ok += 1

        z = convolve(group, u, v)
        if not support(z):
            conv_zero += 1
        elif is_extremal(group, z):
            conv_ok += 1

    print(f"random extremal pairs tested on Z/12   : {pairs}")
    print(f"pointwise products: zero {prod_zero:>3}, extremal {prod_ok:>3},"
          f" other {pairs - prod_zero - prod_ok:>3}")
    print(f"convolutions      : zero {conv_zero:>3}, extremal {conv_ok:>3},"
          f" other {pairs - conv_zero - conv_ok:>3}")

    k_sub = subgroup_generated(group, [(4,)])
    f = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, (1,), (3,), 1 + 0j)

    sizes = [len(support(g))]
    for _ in range(4):
        g = convolve(group, f, g)
        sizes.append(len(support(g)))
    print(f"\nconvolution powers of a fixed extremal: support sizes {sizes}"
          " (conserved)")

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Elem = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Func = Dict[Elem, complex]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Group arithmetic and characters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elem]:
    """All elements of Z/n_1 x ... x Z/n_r, in lexicographic order."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The order |G| of the group."""
    n = 1
    for m in group:
        n *= m
    return n


def add(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group addition."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def sub(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group subtraction."""
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def zero(group: Group) -> Elem:
    """The neutral element."""
    return tuple(0 for _ in group)


def character(group: Group, k: Elem, x: Elem) -> complex:
    """The character psi_k evaluated at x: exp(2*pi*i * sum k_j x_j / n_j)."""
    phase = sum(2.0 * cmath.pi * (kj * xj) / nj for kj, xj, nj in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * phase)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The discrete Fourier transform
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    """fhat(k) = sum_x conj(psi_k(x)) f(x), indexed by the dual element k."""
    els = elements(group)
    out: Func = {}
    for k in els:
        total = 0j
        for x in els:
            fx = f.get(x, 0j)
            if fx != 0:
                total += character(group, k, x).conjugate() * fx
        out[k] = total
    return out


def idft(group: Group, fhat: Func) -> Func:
    """Inverse transform: f(x) = (1/N) sum_k psi_k(x) fhat(k)."""
    els = elements(group)
    n = order(group)
    return {
        x: sum(character(group, k, x) * fhat.get(k, 0j) for k in els) / n for x in els
    }


def support(f: Func, tol: float = TOL) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The set of points where f is (numerically) nonzero."""
    return {x for x, v in f.items() if abs(v) > tol}


def uncertainty_product(group: Group, f: Func) -> int:
    """|supp f| * |supp fhat|."""
    return len(support(f)) * len(support(dft(group, f)))


def is_extremal(group: Group, f: Func) -> bool:
    """True when |supp f| * |supp fhat| = |G| (and f is nonzero)."""
    if not support(f):
        return False
    return uncertainty_product(group, f) == order(group)


def convolve(group: Group, u: Func, v: Func) -> Func:
    """(u * v)(x) = sum_y u(y) v(x - y)."""
    els = elements(group)
    return {
        x: sum(u.get(y, 0j) * v.get(sub(group, x, y), 0j) for y in els) for x in els
    }


def pointwise(u: Func, v: Func) -> Func:
    """Pointwise product."""
    return {x: u.get(x, 0j) * v.get(x, 0j) for x in set(u) | set(v)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subgroups, cosets, coset modulations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def subgroup_generated(group: Group, gens: Iterable[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The subgroup of G generated by the given elements (closure by BFS)."""
    seen: Set[Elem] = {zero(group)}
    frontier: List[Elem] = [zero(group)]
    gens = list(gens)
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for g in gens:
            y = add(group, x, g)
            if y not in seen:
                seen.add(y)
                frontier.append(y)
    return seen


def all_subgroups(group: Group) -> List[Set[Elem]]:
    """All subgroups of G, obtained by closing every subset of generators
    of size at most the rank + 1 (exhaustive for the small groups used here)."""
    els = elements(group)
    found: Set[frozenset] = set()
    for r in range(0, min(3, len(els)) + 1):
        for gens in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            found.add(frozenset(subgroup_generated(group, gens)))
    return [set(s) for s in sorted(found, key=lambda s: (len(s), sorted(s)))]


def annihilator(group: Group, subgroup: Set[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """K^perp = { k : psi_k(x) = 1 for all x in K }, as a set of dual indices."""
    return {
        k
        for k in elements(group)
        if all(abs(character(group, k, x) - 1.0) < TOL for x in subgroup)
    }


def coset_modulation(
    group: Group, subgroup: Set[Elem], a: Elem, chi: Elem, c: complex
) -> Func:
    """f(x) = c * psi_chi(x) for x in a + K, and 0 elsewhere."""
    cos = {add(group, a, k) for k in subgroup}
    return {
        x: (c * character(group, chi, x) if x in cos else 0j) for x in elements(group)
    }


def difference_set(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """S - S = { x - y : x, y in S }."""
    return {sub(group, x, y) for x in s for y in s}


def is_coset(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """A nonempty S is a coset iff |S - S| = |S| (equivalently, iff S is
    closed under the parallelogram operation (x, y, z) -> x - y + z)."""
    return bool(s) and len(difference_set(group, s)) == len(s)


def is_parallelogram_closed(group: Group, s: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """Direct test of closure under (x, y, z) -> x - y + z."""
    return bool(s) and all(
        add(group, sub(group, x, y), z) in s for x in s for y in s for z in s
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structure extraction (Algorithm 2 of the paper)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def extract_structure(
    group: Group, f: Func
) -> Optional[Tuple[Set[Elem], Elem, Elem, complex]]:
    """For an extremal f, recover (K, a, chi, c) with f = c * psi_chi * 1_{a+K}.

    Returns None if f is not extremal.  The subgroup is recovered purely
    combinatorially, as the difference set of the support; the character index
    is then found by matching phases on the support.
    """
    if not is_extremal(group, f):
        return None
    s = support(f)
    a = sorted(s)[0]
    k_sub = difference_set(group, s)
    c_times_chi_a = f[a]
    for chi in elements(group):
        c = c_times_chi_a * character(group, chi, a).conjugate()
        candidate = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, a, chi, c)
        if all(abs(candidate[x] - f.get(x, 0j)) < 1e-7 for x in elements(group)):
            return k_sub, a, chi, c
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Poisson pairs (Definition 3.3, Lemma 3.4, Corollary 3.8)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def poisson_holds_for(group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem], f: Func) -> bool:
    """Check N * sum_{x in S} f(x) = |S| * sum_{k in T} fhat(k) for one f."""
    n = order(group)
    fhat = dft(group, f)
    lhs = n * sum(f.get(x, 0j) for x in s)
    rhs = len(s) * sum(fhat[k] for k in t)
    return abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-7


def poisson_dirac_test(group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """The finite certificate: check only the |G| Dirac identities
    N * 1_S(y) = |S| * sum_{k in T} psi_k(y)."""
    n = order(group)
    for y in elements(group):
        lhs = n * (1.0 if y in s else 0.0)
        rhs = len(s) * sum(character(group, k, y) for k in t)
        if abs(lhs - rhs) > 1e-7:
            return False
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def divisors(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """All positive divisors of n, ascending."""
    return [d for d in range(1, n + 1) if n % d == 0]


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 2: exhaustive verification on Z/4
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_exhaustive_z4() -> None:
    banner("2. Exhaustive census on Z/4 over the values {0, 1, -1, i, -i}")
    group: Group = (4,)
    els = elements(group)
    values: Sequence[complex] = (0j, 1 + 0j, -1 + 0j, 1j, -1j)

    total = 0
    nonzero = 0
    bound_ok = True
    extremals: List[Func] = []
    size_hist: Dict[int, int] = {d: 0 for d in range(5)}

    for combo in itertools.product(values, repeat=len(els)):
        f: Func = dict(zip(els, combo))
        total += 1
        s = support(f)
        if not s:
            continue
        nonzero += 1
        prod = uncertainty_product(group, f)
        if prod < 4:
            bound_ok = False
        if prod == 4:
            extremals.append(f)
            size_hist[len(s)] += 1

    print(f"functions tested / nonzero            : {total} / {nonzero}")
    print(f"uncertainty bound |supp f||supp fhat| >= 4 holds everywhere : {bound_ok}")
    print(f"number of extremals                   : {len(extremals)}")
    print("support-size distribution of extremals: "
          + ", ".join(f"size {d}: {size_hist[d]}" for d in range(5)))
    print("  (no extremal of support size 3, because 3 does not divide 4)")

    all_cosets = all(is_coset(group, support(f)) for f in extremals)
    flat = all(
        len({round(abs(f[x]), 9) for x in support(f)}) == 1 for f in extremals
    )
    freq_cosets = all(
        is_coset(group, support(dft(group, f))) for f in extremals
    )
    print(f"every extremal support is a coset     : {all_cosets}")
    print(f"every extremal is flat on its support : {flat}")
    print(f"every frequency support is a coset    : {freq_cosets}")

    bad: Func = {(0,): 1 + 0j, (1,): 1 + 0j, (2,): 0j, (3,): 0j}
    print(f"\nthe non-coset support {{0,1}}: product = "
          f"{uncertainty_product(group, bad)} > 4, so not extremal")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_extremal_spectrum() -> None:
    banner("3. The extremal spectrum of G equals the divisor set of |G|")
    for group in [(4,), (2, 2), (6,), (12,), (6, 2)]:
        n = order(group)
        achievable = sorted({len(k) for k in all_subgroups(group)})
        # realise each size by an explicit extremal function and check it
        realised = []
        for k_sub in all_subgroups(group):
            f = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, zero(group), zero(group), 1 + 0j)
            if is_extremal(group, f):
                realised.append(len(k_sub))
        name = " x ".join(f"Z/{m}" for m in group)
        print(f"{name:<14} |G| = {n:>3}   subgroup orders {achievable}"
              f"   divisors {divisors(n)}")
        assert achievable == divisors(n) == sorted(set(realised))
    print("\nEvery divisor is realised by an explicit extremal function, and no"
          "\nother size occurs -- the extremal spectrum theorem.")

    group: Group = (12,)

    print("-" * 48)

        divides = n % s == 0

    print("\nEmpirical check for s = 5 on Z/12 (random 5-point supports):")

def demo_algebra_closure() -> None:
    banner("7. Products and convolutions of extremals are zero or extremal")
    group: Group = (12,)
    subs = all_subgroups(group)
    import random

    random.seed(1234)

    pairs = 0
    prod_zero = 0
    conv_zero = 0
    prod_ok = 0
    conv_ok = 0
    for _ in range(60):
        k1 = random.choice(subs)
        k2 = random.choice(subs)
        u = coset_modulation(
            group, k1, random.choice(elements(group)),
            random.choice(elements(group)), complex(random.uniform(0.5, 2))
        )
        v = coset_modulation(
            group, k2, random.choice(elements(group)),
            random.choice(elements(group)), complex(0, random.uniform(0.5, 2))
        )
        pairs += 1

        w = pointwise(u, v)
        if not support(w):
            prod_zero += 1
        elif is_extremal(group, w):
            prod_ok += 1

        z = convolve(group, u, v)
        if not support(z):
            conv_zero += 1
        elif is_extremal(group, z):
            conv_ok += 1

    print(f"random extremal pairs tested on Z/12   : {pairs}")
    print(f"pointwise products: zero {prod_zero:>3}, extremal {prod_ok:>3},"
          f" other {pairs - prod_zero - prod_ok:>3}")
    print(f"convolutions      : zero {conv_zero:>3}, extremal {conv_ok:>3},"
          f" other {pairs - conv_zero - conv_ok:>3}")

    # convolution powers preserve the support size exactly
    k_sub = subgroup_generated(group, [(4,)])
    f = coset_modulation(group, k_sub, (1,), (3,), 1 + 0j)
    g = dict(f)
    sizes = [len(support(g))]
    for _ in range(4):
        g = convolve(group, f, g)
        sizes.append(len(support(g)))
    print(f"\nconvolution powers of a fixed extremal: support sizes {sizes}"
          " (conserved)")

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Tuple

# Gaussian integers as pairs (re, im)
GI = Tuple[int, int]

N: int = 4
ZERO: GI = (0, 0)
UNITS: Tuple[GI, ...] = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))


def gadd(z: GI, w: GI) -> GI:
    """Addition in Z[i]."""
    return (z[0] + w[0], z[1] + w[1])


def gmul(z: GI, w: GI) -> GI:
    """Multiplication in Z[i]."""
    return (z[0] * w[0] - z[1] * w[1], z[0] * w[1] + z[1] * w[0])


def gconj(z: GI) -> GI:
    """Complex conjugation."""
    return (z[0], -z[1])


def gnorm(z: GI) -> int:
    """Squared modulus |z|^2, an ordinary integer."""
    return z[0] * z[0] + z[1] * z[1]


def char4(k: int, x: int) -> GI:
    """The character psi_k(x) = i^{k x} of Z/4, exactly."""
    return [(1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (0, -1)][(k * x) % 4]


def dft4(f: List[GI]) -> List[GI]:
    """fhat(k) = sum_x conj(psi_k(x)) f(x), in exact Gaussian arithmetic."""
    out: List[GI] = []
    for k in range(N):
        acc: GI = ZERO
        for x in range(N):
            acc = gadd(acc, gmul(gconj(char4(k, x)), f[x]))
        out.append(acc)
    return out


def supp(f: List[GI]) -> Set[int]:
    """Exact support."""
    return {i for i, z in enumerate(f) if z != ZERO}


def is_coset(s: Set[int]) -> bool:
    """Closure under the parallelogram operation (x, y, z) -> x - y + z."""
    return bool(s) and all((x - y + z) % N in s for x in s for y in s for z in s)


def convolve(u: List[GI], v: List[GI]) -> List[GI]:
    """(u * v)(x) = sum_y u(y) v(x - y)."""
    out: List[GI] = []
    for x in range(N):
        acc: GI = ZERO
        for y in range(N):
            acc = gadd(acc, gmul(u[y], v[(x - y) % N]))
        out.append(acc)
    return out


def pointwise(u: List[GI], v: List[GI]) -> List[GI]:
    """Pointwise product."""
    return [gmul(a, b) for a, b in zip(u, v)]


def extremal(f: List[GI]) -> bool:
    """|supp f| * |supp fhat| = 4 (and f nonzero)."""
    s = supp(f)
    return bool(s) and len(s) * len(supp(dft4(f))) == N


def main() -> None:
    total = 0
    nonzero = 0
    bound_ok = True
    extremals: List[List[GI]] = []
    hist: Dict[int, int] = {d: 0 for d in range(N + 1)}

    for combo in itertools.product(UNITS, repeat=N):
        f = list(combo)
        total += 1
        s = supp(f)
        if not s:
            continue
        nonzero += 1
        prod = len(s) * len(supp(dft4(f)))
        if prod < N:
            bound_ok = False
        if prod == N:
            extremals.append(f)
            hist[len(s)] += 1

    print("Exhaustive census on Z/4 with values in {0, 1, -1, i, -i}")
    print("-" * 62)
    print(f"functions tested / nonzero                 : {total} / {nonzero}")
    print(f"uncertainty bound holds everywhere         : {bound_ok}")
    print(f"number of extremals                        : {len(extremals)}")
    print("support-size distribution of the extremals : "
          + ", ".join(f"{d}:{hist[d]}" for d in range(N + 1)))
    print("   (size 3 is absent because 3 does not divide 4)")

    print(f"every extremal support is a coset          : "
          f"{all(is_coset(supp(f)) for f in extremals)}")
    print(f"every extremal is flat on its support      : "
          f"{all(len({gnorm(f[x]) for x in supp(f)}) == 1 for f in extremals)}")
    print(f"every frequency support is a coset         : "

          f"{len(supp(bad)) * len(supp(dft4(bad)))} > {N}, hence not extremal")

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
from typing import Dict, List, NamedTuple, Optional, Set, Tuple

Elem = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Func = Dict[Elem, complex]

TOL: float = 1e-9


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elem]:
    """All group elements, lexicographically ordered."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The group order |G|."""
    n = 1
    for m in group:
        n *= m
    return n


def sub(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group subtraction x - y."""
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def add(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group addition x + y."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def character(group: Group, k: Elem, x: Elem) -> complex:
    """psi_k(x) = exp(2*pi*i * sum_j k_j x_j / n_j)."""
    phase = sum(2.0 * cmath.pi * (kj * xj) / nj for kj, xj, nj in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * phase)


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    """fhat(k) = sum_x conj(psi_k(x)) f(x).  Cost O(|G|^2)."""
    els = elements(group)
    return {
        k: sum(character(group, k, x).conjugate() * f.get(x, 0j) for x in els)
        for k in els
    }


def support(f: Func, tol: float = TOL) -> Set[Elem]:
    """{x : |f(x)| > tol}."""
    return {x for x, v in f.items() if abs(v) > tol}


class Audit(NamedTuple):
    """Result of an uncertainty audit."""

    space_support: int
    freq_support: int
    product: int
    group_order: int
    extremal: bool
    subgroup: Optional[Set[Elem]]
    representative: Optional[Elem]
    character_index: Optional[Elem]
    scalar: Optional[complex]


def audit(group: Group, f: Func) -> Audit:
    """Full uncertainty audit with structure extraction when extremal."""
    n = order(group)
    s = support(f)
    t = support(dft(group, f))
    product = len(s) * len(t)
    extremal = bool(s) and product == n
    if not extremal:
        return Audit(len(s), len(t), product, n, False, None, None, None, None)

    # The subgroup is the difference set of the support (a combinatorial
    # description of an analytically defined object).
    k_sub = {sub(group, x, y) for x in s for y in s}
    a = sorted(s)[0]
    # The phase f(x)/f(a) equals chi(x - a); match against every character.
    for chi in elements(group):
        c = f[a] * character(group, chi, a).conjugate()
        ok = all(
            abs(f.get(x, 0j) - (c * character(group, chi, x) if x in s else 0j)) < 1e-7
            for x in elements(group)
        )
        if ok:
            return Audit(len(s), len(t), product, n, True, k_sub, a, chi, c)
    raise RuntimeError("extremal function with no coset-modulation form")

import cmath
import itertools

Group = Tuple[int, ...]

def add(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group addition."""

def character(group: Group, k: Elem, x: Elem) -> complex:
    """psi_k(x)."""
    phase = sum(2.0 * cmath.pi * (kj * xj) / nj for kj, xj, nj in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * phase)


def dirac_certificate(group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem]) -> bool:
    """Verify the |G| Dirac identities.  Cost O(|G| |T|)."""
    n = order(group)
    for y in elements(group):
        lhs = n * (1.0 if y in s else 0.0)
        rhs = len(s) * sum(character(group, k, y) for k in t)
        if abs(lhs - rhs) > TOL:
            return False
    return True


def pre_annihilator(group: Group, t: Set[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """{y in G : psi_k(y) = 1 for all k in T} -- always a subgroup."""
    return {
        y
        for y in elements(group)
        if all(abs(character(group, k, y) - 1.0) < TOL for k in t)
    }


def poisson_structure(
    group: Group, s: Set[Elem], t: Set[Elem]
) -> Optional[Tuple[Set[Elem], Set[Elem]]]:
    """If (S, T) is a Poisson pair, return (subgroup, annihilator) = (S, T);
    otherwise return None.  The subgroup is recomputed independently, as the
    pre-annihilator of T, and checked against S."""
    if not s or not dirac_certificate(group, s, t):
        return None
    h = pre_annihilator(group, t)
    assert h == s, "the rigidity theorem guarantees S is the pre-annihilator of T"
    assert len(s) * len(t) == order(group), "and that |S| |T| = |G|"
    return s, t

import itertools
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Tuple

Elem = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The group order."""
    n = 1
    for m in group:
        n *= m
    return n


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elem]:
    """All group elements."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def add(group: Group, x: Elem, y: Elem) -> Elem:
    """Group addition."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def cyclic_subgroup(group: Group, g: Elem) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The subgroup generated by a single element."""
    out = {tuple(0 for _ in group)}
    cur = g
    while cur not in out:
        out.add(cur)
        cur = add(group, cur, g)
    return out


def subgroup_generated(group: Group, gens: List[Elem]) -> Set[Elem]:
    """The subgroup generated by a list of elements (breadth-first closure)."""
    out: Set[Elem] = {tuple(0 for _ in group)}
    frontier = [tuple(0 for _ in group)]
    while frontier:
        x = frontier.pop()
        for g in gens:
            y = add(group, x, g)
            if y not in out:
                out.add(y)
                frontier.append(y)
    return out


def subgroup_of_order(group: Group, d: int) -> Set[Elem]:
    """Construct a subgroup of order d dividing |G| -- a constructive form of
    the converse of Lagrange's theorem for finite abelian groups.

    Strategy (mirroring the inductive proof): greedily adjoin elements whose
    generated subgroup keeps the order a divisor of d, until the order is d.
    Terminates because a finite abelian group of order divisible by a prime p
    contains an element of order p (Cauchy), so progress is always possible.
    """
    n = order(group)
    assert n % d == 0, "d must divide |G|"
    current: Set[Elem] = {tuple(0 for _ in group)}
    gens: List[Elem] = []
    while len(current) < d:
        progressed = False
        for g in elements(group):
            if g in current:
                continue
            cand = subgroup_generated(group, gens + [g])
            if d % len(cand) == 0 and len(cand) > len(current):
                gens.append(g)
                current = cand
                progressed = True
                break
        if not progressed:  # pragma: no cover -- excluded by the theorem
            raise RuntimeError("no subgroup of the requested order")
    return current


def divisors(n: int) -> List[int]:
    """All positive divisors of n."""
    return [d for d in range(1, n + 1) if n % d == 0]


def extremal_spectrum(group: Group) -> List[int]:
    """The achievable support sizes of extremal functions on G."""
    n = order(group)
    return [d for d in divisors(n) if len(subgroup_of_order(group, d)) == d]


def guaranteed_product(n: int, s: int) -> int:
    """The sharpened lower bound for |supp f| * |supp fhat| given |supp f| = s."""
    return n if n % s == 0 else n + (s - n % s)

    $("k").max = String(N - 1);
    if (kChar > N - 1) { kChar = 0; $("k").value = "0"; $("klab").textContent = "0"; }
  }

  function signal() {
    const re = new Array(N).fill(0), im = new Array(N).fill(0);
    for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
      if (!on[x]) continue;

      if (phaseMode === 1) th = 2 * Math.PI * kChar * x / N;
      if (phaseMode === 2) th = rnd[x];

    const d = new Set();

    $("sf").textContent = T.length;
    $("pr").textContent = prod;

    $("lb").textContent = s === 0 ? "—" : lower;

    const badge = $("badge");

    else if (prod === N) { badge.className = "badge yes"; badge.textContent = "EXTREMAL: product = N"; }
    else { badge.className = "badge no"; badge.textContent = "not extremal: product = " + prod + " > " + N; }

  function drawBars(cv, f, color) {

    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);

the <code>N</code> Dirac spikes, which turns the identity into
<code>N · 1<sub>S</sub>(y) = |S| · Σ<sub>k∈T</sub> ψ<sub>k</sub>(y)</code>. The bars show
the residual of that finite test at each <code>y</code>. Only subgroup /
annihilator pairs ever pass — that is the rigidity theorem, and you can hunt
for a counterexample here.
